lxc_564466e1ae67f623.text: Coffee bags and café menus often use words such as blend, single origin, light roast, and dark roast.

lxc_2f754e1c7e129995.text: You will learn what these words mean and how to explain a coffee to a customer in clear English.

lxc_56fe4370119b344f.text: A blend combines two or more coffees.

lxc_910a673e04bd5f6c.text: The coffees may come from different farms, regions, countries, plant varieties, or processing methods.

lxc_9ecd77767f031a57.text: A roaster chooses the parts carefully to make one planned flavour.

lxc_f01438be3e176d13.text: Blends can help a café offer a stable house coffee through the year.

lxc_6de3c753121f62c2.text: If one seasonal coffee changes, the roaster can adjust another part of the blend.

lxc_97a1f11a35f1ddd8.text: Many espresso blends are also designed to keep a clear coffee taste when milk is added.

lxc_e40f394debe2424c.text: They may have familiar chocolate, caramel, or nut flavours that work well in a flat white or latte.

lxc_5fdfe1b7b89de59c.text: Single origin means the coffee comes from one defined origin.

lxc_9ccfbb1cd9cdbd5c.text: The origin can be a country, a region, a cooperative, one farm, or even one small lot.

lxc_5c5afd168f33035b.text: The label should tell the customer how specific the origin is.

lxc_f82c86944b06cf82.text: Cafés often serve single-origin coffee when they want people to notice a special flavour.

lxc_927b50ae3f7bc3fc.text: One coffee may remind people of berries or citrus.

lxc_f36f85f2a2a1a4cc.text: Another may have chocolate, nuts, or flowers.

lxc_24a80ad7cf681933.text: They do not usually mean that berries, chocolate, or flowers were added to the beans.

lxc_5bc04e8d45257251.text: Roasting changes green coffee into brown, aromatic coffee.

lxc_b212c3122dbc1153.text: A light roast usually keeps more of the coffee's original fruit, flower, and bright character.

lxc_08742239350cd88d.text: It may also feel lighter in the mouth.

lxc_89afb442ec1a2820.text: A dark roast develops more roasted flavours.

lxc_00841bbdab3661d1.text: It may taste more bitter, smoky, or like dark chocolate.

lxc_69966a053d36989e.text: Light does not always mean weak, and dark does not always mean stronger caffeine.

lxc_b9cb4e1b55fd0c0d.text: Roast level mainly tells us how far the roaster developed the beans.

lxc_dc8c1e4abe9e9a1d.text: The final strength in the cup also depends on the dose, water, recipe, and brewing method.

lxc_d1340e73513bbdfe.text: Coffee professionals often use the word acidity for a bright, lively taste.

lxc_73ea1d8018c73bf1.text: Pleasant acidity can remind people of orange, apple, berries, or sparkling fruit.

lxc_b07e067dba494047.text: It can make a coffee feel fresh and interesting.

lxc_5d00f9eac7e78392.text: It can taste sharp, aggressive, and unbalanced.

lxc_ee07b463f447b46f.text: A poorly made espresso may taste sour because the water did not take enough flavour from the coffee.

lxc_12710c7deaf1c82f.text: However, a fruity light roast can be well made and still have pleasant acidity.

lxc_4d5cb5bc04c99ff6.text: A good barista listens carefully before deciding that a customer dislikes all acidity.

lxc_587c63162a6b679f.text: - This single origin is lighter and fruitier.

lxc_040b8d4d4caaa25b.text: - It is bright and balanced, not sharply sour.
